Loss-of-function variants in VHL lead to impaired ubiquitination and degradation of HIF-alpha. Stabilization of HIF then leads to increased erythropoiesis (polycythemia) and alterations in hemoglobin, contributing to the phenotypes of both Chuvash polycythemia and obsolete hemoglobin, high altitude adaptation.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in VHL that are clearly associated with gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in both diseases, or the discovery of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways driving each condition. _(variant: rs61760635)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of VHL and HIF dysregulation in these conditions could inform therapeutic strategies targeting the HIF pathway for polycythemic disorders and potentially for conditions related to high-altitude adaptation.
